A1-1-0.title: ¿His, her, its o their?
A1-1-0.question: ¿Quién es el dueño de la cosa?

branches.example: Mario and his mother.
Ana and her brother.
The dog and its bed.
Luis and Sara and their house.

items.note: his = de él; her = de ella. Mira al dueño, no a la cosa.
they are = ellos son; their = de ellos.
it’s = it is; its = de eso (sin apóstrofo).
you’re = you are; your = tu.

steps.label: Pregunta sí/no
steps.change: Are pasa delante de you. No usamos do.

steps.label: Pregunta Wh
steps.change: La palabra Wh va al principio y luego are + sujeto.

steps.label: Respuesta corta
steps.change: Con yes no se contrae: no se dice Yes, I’m.

branches.if: Solo un sí o un no
branches.example: Are you tired? — Yes, I am.
Where is your school? — It’s in Suba.

A1-2-0.title: De afirmación a pregunta con does

steps.label: Pregunta sí/no
steps.change: Aparece does y el verbo pierde la -s.

A1-2-0.title: ¿Do o does?
A1-2-0.question: ¿Cuál es el sujeto de la pregunta?

branches.if: I, you, we, they (o varias personas)
branches.example: Where do your parents live?

branches.if: He, she, it (o un nombre: Ana, my brother)
branches.example: Where does Ana live?

items.note: do con you; does con he. El verbo work no cambia.
La -s pasa del verbo a does.
watches lleva -es; con doesn’t vuelve a watch.
have cambia a has con he, she, it.

A1-2-1.title: Tiempo en el reloj y el calendario

branches.example: I start at 6:30. I sleep at night.
The meeting is on Friday, on 3 May.

branches.if: Un mes, un año o una parte del día
branches.example: I travel in April. I study in the evening.

items.note: at = exacto; around = más o menos.
until = hasta (ahí termino); after = después de (empiezo luego).
before = antes; after = después.
Ojo: in the morning / in the afternoon, pero at night.

A1-3-0.title: ¿This, that, these o those?
A1-3-0.question: ¿Está cerca o lejos? ¿Es una o son varias?

branches.example: This pen is mine.
That house is big.
These shoes are new.
Those mountains are beautiful.

items.note: this = cerca de mí; that = lejos de mí.
En plural: these + are.
Plural y lejos: those + are.
one / ones evita repetir el sustantivo.

branches.example: A bus is cheaper than a taxi.
English is easier than Chinese.

branches.if: Largo, de dos sílabas o más
branches.example: A taxi is more expensive than a bus.
Today is better than yesterday.

items.note: hot duplica la t: hotter.

items.b: This bag is cheaper than that one.
items.note: Corto: + -er + than.

items.b: The hotel is more comfortable than the hostel.
items.note: Largo: more + adjetivo.

items.b: My English is better than my brother’s.
items.note: good → better. Nunca more good ni more better.

steps.label: Con pronombres
steps.change: Ana hace la acción → she. Luis la recibe → him.

steps.label: Al revés
steps.change: Ahora Ana recibe la acción: she → her.

steps.label: Pregunta
steps.change: Después del verbo va el pronombre objeto.

A1-4-0.title: ¿I o me? ¿he o him?
A1-4-0.question: ¿Dónde está el pronombre en la oración?

branches.if: Antes del verbo: hace la acción
branches.use: I, you, he, she, it, we, they
branches.example: He calls me every day.

branches.if: Después del verbo: recibe la acción
branches.use: me, you, him, her, it, us, them
branches.example: I call him every day.

branches.if: Después de una preposición (with, to, for)
branches.use: me, you, him, her, it, us, them
branches.example: Come with us!

items.note: Cambia quién llama y quién recibe la llamada.
we / they hacen la acción; us / them la reciben.
Después de to va el pronombre objeto: to me, to her.
La persona va primero y después la cosa.

A1-4-1.title: De pedir a ofrecer con amabilidad

steps.label: Educado
steps.change: I’d like (= I would like) es más amable.

steps.label: Ofrecer
steps.change: Would pasa delante de you para preguntar.

branches.example: Would you like some water?
Would you like to come with us?

branches.if: Su gusto en general, no una oferta
branches.example: Do you like coffee? — Yes, I love it.

items.note: Would you like = te ofrezco ahora; Do you like = ¿te gusta en general?
I’d like = quisiera (ahora); I like = me gusta (siempre).

items.a: Would you like to sit here?
items.note: Con acción: to + verbo. Con cosa: el sustantivo directo.
I’d love to es más entusiasta: me encantaría.

A1-5-0.title: Del presente continuo a la pregunta

items.note: Presente simple = rutina; presente continuo = ahora / hoy.
What do you do? = ¿a qué te dedicas?; What are you doing? = ¿qué estás haciendo?
every day = hábito; right now = en este momento.
Se quita la -e final; se duplica la consonante después de una vocal corta.

items.example: All my friends have a phone.
Nearly all my cousins are older than me.
A lot of people work at home.
Do many students walk to school?
Some students are late.
Not many people speak French here.
Few students arrive late.
No one is at home.

A1-5-1.title: ¿A lot of, many o no one?
A1-5-1.question: ¿Qué tipo de oración es?

branches.example: A lot of people use the metro.
Do many people use the metro? — Not many.
No one knows the answer.

items.note: Usa of solo si sigue my, the, these…

items.b: Nearly all my friends live here.
items.note: nearly all = casi todos, no el 100 %.
not many = pocos; no one = nadie.
no one y everyone van con verbo en singular: is.

items.example: I always have breakfast.
I almost always walk to work.
I usually get up at six.
We often eat out on Fridays.
Sometimes I take a taxi.
She hardly ever answers her phone.
He never eats fish.

branches.example: I always study at night.

branches.if: El verbo to be (am, is, are)
branches.example: He is usually late.
I don’t usually work on Sundays.

steps.label: Con verbo normal
steps.change: El adverbio va antes del verbo principal.

steps.label: Con to be
steps.change: Con to be, el adverbio va después.

steps.label: Negativa
steps.change: En la negativa va después de don’t.

branches.example: How often do you swim? — Twice a week.
How long is the class? — About an hour.

branches.if: Qué tan bien hace algo (con un verbo)
branches.example: How well does she sing? — Very well.

branches.if: Qué tan bueno es en algo (con un sustantivo)
branches.example: How good is he at maths? — Not very good.

items.example: She speaks English really well.
He cooks very well.
I play the guitar quite well.
I dance, but not very well.
I sing badly!

items.note: often = cada cuánto (Twice a week); long = cuánto tiempo (For an hour).
good va con be; well va con otros verbos.

items.b: How good are you at cooking?
items.note: Las dos preguntan por habilidad: well + verbo; good at + -ing.

steps.label: Pregunta
steps.change: Did va primero; work vuelve a la base.

items.note: go → went: es irregular.
Consonante + y → -ied.
Se duplica la consonante: stopped.
Con did, el verbo va en base (see); sin did, en pasado (saw).

branches.example: It was cold last night.
We were at home all day.

branches.if: Hay una cosa / hay varias (en pasado)
branches.example: There was a party. There were many people.

A1-7-1.title: Del presente al pasado con to be

steps.label: Pregunta
steps.sentence: **Was** she at home yesterday? — Yes, she **was**.

items.a: Did you go to the party?
items.note: Acción (go) → did; estado o lugar (be) → were, sin did.
Con otro verbo: didn’t + base; con be: wasn’t.
Una cosa → was; varias → were.
he → was; they → were.

branches.example: There is a bank on my street.

branches.if: Algo que no se cuenta (noise, water)
branches.example: There is a lot of traffic.
There are two parks near here.

branches.use: Are there any…? / There aren’t any…
branches.example: Are there any shops? — No, there aren’t any.
How many rooms are there?
How much time do you need?

A1-8-1.title: A few, few, a little, little

items.a: I have a few friends here.
items.note: a few = algunos (positivo); few = casi ninguno (negativo).
a little = un poco; little = casi nada.
many con plural; much con incontable.
shops se cuentan; traffic no.

branches.example: What does he look like? — He’s tall with short hair.
What is he like? — He’s very friendly.
Who does she look like? — Her mother.
How does she look? — She looks tired.

items.note: be like = personalidad; look like = físico.
La respuesta a look like no lleva like: He is tall.
Rasgos (eyes, hair) → has; descripción general → is.
How does she look? = cómo se ve hoy; look like = cómo es siempre.

steps.label: Dos oraciones
steps.sentence: The woman **is standing** near the door. She’s my aunt.

steps.label: Una oración
steps.sentence: The woman **standing** near the door is my aunt.
steps.change: Quitamos is y el verbo con -ing va justo después del sustantivo.

steps.label: Con the one
steps.sentence: **The one standing** near the door is my aunt.
steps.change: the one reemplaza a the woman.

A1-9-1.title: ¿Cómo señalo a alguien sin el dedo?
A1-9-1.question: ¿Qué está haciendo o qué tiene la persona?

branches.example: the one reading a book

branches.if: Lleva una prenda o tiene un objeto
branches.use: the one in… / the one with…
branches.example: the one in the black coat, the one with glasses
the ones waiting outside

items.en: the one sitting at the back

A1-10-0.title: Already y yet en su lugar

steps.label: Con already
steps.change: already va entre have y el participio.

steps.label: Pregunta con yet
steps.change: have pasa delante de you; yet al final.

branches.example: She has already left.
She hasn’t left yet.
Has she left yet?

branches.if: No: solo importa la experiencia o el resultado
branches.example: I have been to Cartagena.

branches.if: Sí: yesterday, last week, in 2019, ago
branches.example: I went to Cartagena in 2019.
When did you go?

steps.label: Detalle con fecha
steps.change: Al decir cuándo, pasamos al pasado simple.

steps.label: Seguimos en pasado
steps.change: La historia sigue en pasado simple.

items.note: Sin fecha → presente perfecto; con fecha → pasado simple.
been = fue y volvió; gone = todavía está allá.

items.b: Did you see the film last night?
items.note: last night pide pasado simple.
never = en toda mi vida; in 2020 = un momento terminado.

items.example: The hotel is a bit expensive.
The park is quite far.
The food is very good.
The room is really clean.
This bird is extremely rare.

A1-11-0.title: ¿And, but, so o because?
A1-11-0.question: ¿Qué relación hay entre las dos ideas?

branches.example: It’s cheap and very clean.
It’s small but really comfortable.

branches.if: La segunda idea es el resultado
branches.example: It was cheap, so we bought two.

branches.if: La segunda idea es la razón
branches.example: I love this park because it’s quiet.

items.a: It was late, so we left.
items.b: We left because it was late.
items.note: so → resultado; because → razón.
a bit solo va con adjetivos negativos: no se dice a bit beautiful.
quite = bastante; really = muy.

branches.example: You can take the bus from here.

branches.if: Es un consejo, una buena idea
branches.example: You should visit the museum.
You shouldn’t go there at night.

items.note: can = es posible; should = te lo recomiendo.
can’t = no está permitido; shouldn’t = no es buena idea.
could suena más suave que can.
Ninguno lleva -s: he should, he can.

branches.if: It’s a good idea / It’s better / The best way is
branches.example: It’s a good idea to book early.

branches.if: need, want, try, plan, hope, decide
branches.example: You need to bring your ID.
I recommend visiting the museum.
You should book early.

steps.label: Frase fija
steps.sentence: **It’s a good idea to book** in advance.
steps.change: It’s a good idea + to + verbo.

steps.label: La mejor manera
steps.sentence: **The best way is to book** in advance.
steps.change: The best way is + to + verbo.

items.b: It’s a good idea to visit the museum.
items.note: recommend + -ing; It’s a good idea + to.
should sin to; need con to.
En la negativa, not va antes de to.

items.example: Open the window.
Can you open the window?
Could you open the window, please?
Would you mind opening the window?

branches.if: Pedirle un favor a un amigo
branches.example: Can you pass me the salt?

branches.if: Pedirle un favor a un desconocido o al jefe
branches.example: Could you help me, please?
Could I use your phone?
Should we take a taxi?

items.note: Aquí could no es pasado: es más cortés.
Can I = pido permiso; Can you = pido un favor.
Should we…? pregunta; Let’s propone directamente.

A1-13-0.title: ¿So o neither?
A1-13-0.question: ¿La frase de la otra persona es positiva o negativa?

branches.example: I love pizza. — So do I.
I don’t like fish. — Neither do I.
I love fish. — Oh, I don’t.
I’m hungry. — So am I.
I live here. — So do I.
I saw it. — So did I.
I can swim. — So can I.

items.b: I like it. — So do I.
items.note: El ayudante copia el verbo: am → am; like → do.
Pasado → did; presente perfecto → have.

items.a: I can’t drive. — Neither can I.
items.b: I can’t drive. — I can’t either.
items.note: neither va con verbo afirmativo; either va con verbo negativo.

items.a: I don’t eat meat. — Me neither.
items.b: I don’t eat meat. — Oh, I do.
items.note: Me neither = estoy de acuerdo; Oh, I do = no estoy de acuerdo.

branches.example: Would you like something to eat?
I’d like two tickets, please.

branches.if: Pedir un favor con mucha cortesía
branches.example: Would you mind closing the window?
I’d rather stay at home.

steps.label: Respuesta
steps.change: Significa: no me molesta, con gusto lo hago.

items.note: mind + -ing = ¿te molesta…?; like + to = ¿te gustaría…?

items.a: Would you mind…? — Not at all.
items.note: A Would you mind…? se responde Not at all para decir que sí lo haces.
I’d like es la forma educada de I want.

steps.label: Comparativo
steps.change: Dos cosas: se duplica la t, + -er + than.

steps.label: Superlativo
steps.sentence: Barranquilla is **the hottest of** the three.
steps.change: El número uno del grupo: the + -est + of.

branches.example: The metro is faster than the bus.

branches.if: Tres o más: el número uno
branches.example: Bogotá is the largest city in Colombia.

branches.use: better / the best, worse / the worst
branches.example: This is the best arepa in town.

items.note: in para lugares; of para grupos.
Comparativo: dos cosas; superlativo: el número uno, siempre con the.
Adjetivo largo: more → the most.
good → better → the best. Nunca the most best.

branches.example: How long is the river? — It’s 1,500 km long.

branches.if: La altura de personas o edificios
branches.example: How tall is he? — He’s 1.80 m tall.
How high is Monserrate? — It’s 3,150 m high.
How far is the coast? — About 1,000 km.

items.note: tall para personas y edificios; high para montañas.
long = el largo del puente; far = la distancia hasta el puente.
long = dura dos horas; away = queda a dos horas.

branches.example: I’m going to look for a new job.

branches.if: Ya está acordado, con hora y lugar
branches.example: We’re flying on Sunday at nine.

branches.if: Es una predicción por lo que ves
branches.example: Look at those clouds. It’s going to rain.
The bus leaves at six.

steps.label: Intención
steps.sentence: I**’m going to see** the doctor.
steps.change: Ya es una intención clara: be going to.

steps.label: Cita acordada
steps.sentence: I**’m seeing** the doctor **on Monday at nine**.
steps.change: Con día y hora: presente continuo.

items.a: I’m going to visit my aunt.
items.b: I’m visiting my aunt on Sunday at noon.
items.note: going to = intención; continuo = ya está acordado.
going to = va a llover (predicción); It’s raining = está lloviendo ahora.

items.a: Are you going to study tonight?
items.note: Las dos preguntan por planes; la segunda suena a algo ya organizado.

branches.example: Tell Ana that I’m late.

branches.if: Las palabras o la idea (that…, hello, sorry)
branches.example: Say that you’re sorry.

branches.if: Una orden para pasarle a otro
branches.example: Tell him to wait.

steps.label: Pedirlo con cortesía
steps.sentence: **Could you tell her that** I’m late?
steps.change: could hace la petición más educada.

steps.label: Contarlo después
steps.change: say no lleva persona; el verbo pasa al pasado.

items.note: tell + persona; say va sin persona.
to + verbo = orden; that = información.
Las dos piden repetir: say + lo dicho; tell + persona.

branches.example: I lived in Cali until 2018.

branches.if: Un hábito viejo que ya no existe
branches.example: I used to take the bus.
I live in Bogotá now.

branches.if: Un cambio o resultado que llega hasta hoy
branches.example: The city has grown a lot.

steps.label: Desde entonces
steps.change: Empezó antes y sigue hoy: presente perfecto.

items.a: I lived here for five years.
items.b: I have lived here for five years.
items.note: lived = ya no vivo aquí; have lived = sigo viviendo aquí.
used to = antes sí, ahora no; presente = ahora sí.

items.b: The city has changed a lot.
items.note: Con fecha → pasado simple; sin fecha y con resultado hoy → presente perfecto.

items.example: I’m going to start in March.
I plan to move next year.
I need to find a job.
I want to learn French.
I’d like to study design.
I hope to travel abroad one day.
I decided not to change jobs.

steps.label: Probable
steps.sentence: I **plan to** travel abroad next year.
steps.change: Ya lo estás pensando en serio.

steps.label: Decidido
steps.sentence: I**’m going to** travel abroad in July.

steps.label: Acordado
steps.sentence: I**’m flying** to Madrid on 3 July.
steps.change: Con fecha y tiquete: presente continuo.

items.note: would like to es más educado y menos seguro que want to.

items.b: I decided not to change jobs.
items.note: En la negativa, not va antes de to.

items.a: I’m going to start in March.
items.b: I hope to start one day.
items.note: going to = decidido; hope to = deseo lejano.
